intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunting Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided evening tour away from Reykjavik's light pollution to witness the aurora borealis dancing across the sky. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind this natural phenomenon while capturing stunning photographs.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and swim-up bars while surrounded by dramatic lava fields. Book the Comfort package for access to the main lagoon, towel rental, and one silica mud mask.

experiences.name: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure
experiences.description: Snorkel or dive between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water with visibility up to 100 meters. The surreal blue and green hues of the water make this one of the most unique natural experiences on Earth, guided by certified instructors.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring
experiences.description: Relax in Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a naturally heated geothermal pool surrounded by bubbling hot springs and a small geyser that erupts every few minutes. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic experience offers a peaceful soak amid stunning Icelandic countryside.

experiences.name: Skaftafell Glacier Hike on Vatnajökull
experiences.description: Strap on crampons and hike across Europe's largest glacier with an expert guide. Explore stunning ice formations, deep blue crevasses, and ash layers from ancient volcanic eruptions. The hike offers breathtaking panoramic views of the surrounding black sand plains and mountain peaks.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage. Take the Flybus or a budget shuttle to Reykjavik BSI terminal, then arrange onward travel north toward Siglufjörður. The drive is approximately 4-5 hours via Route 1 and the Héðinsfjörður tunnel. Rest and recover from the flight during the journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Siglufjörður in the early afternoon. Check in early if possible at Hotel Siglunes on Lækjargata 10, or store luggage and take a gentle walk along the harbour front to get oriented. Siglufjörður is a charming small fishing town nestled in a dramatic fjord — explore the colourful wooden houses and the quiet waterfront at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into your room and recover from travel. After dark (which comes early in January), step outside or find a dark spot near the harbour to watch for the Northern Lights — January skies in northern Iceland offer excellent aurora opportunities. Dress in all your warmest layers.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at the airport before departure — budget cafeteria options available at Keflavik.
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches or snacks from a Reykjavik Bonus or Krónan supermarket before heading north to save money on the road.
meals.dinner: Kaffi Rauðka in Siglufjörður — a cosy local café and bar serving hearty Icelandic comfort food at reasonable prices. Try the fish soup.

day_by_day.notes: January days in Siglufjörður have only about 4-5 hours of daylight. The Héðinsfjörður tunnel (opened 2010) makes access much easier. Fill up on fuel before entering the fjord as petrol stations are limited. Pack warm, waterproof clothing — temperatures around 0-5°C with wind chill.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) — one of Iceland's most acclaimed regional museums, documenting the herring fishing boom of the early 20th century. Entry fee is modest and well worth it. Explore the restored harbour buildings and fascinating exhibits about the town's history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike or walk the lower slopes above Siglufjörður for panoramic views of the fjord and surrounding snow-capped mountains. The terrain is dramatic even in winter — stay on marked paths and avoid avalanche-risk areas. Alternatively, walk the full length of the harbour and explore the old fish factory ruins.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights watch from the hillside above town or the harbour pier. Siglufjörður's remote location means very little light pollution — ideal aurora viewing conditions on clear nights. Check the Icelandic Met Office aurora forecast (vedur.is) before heading out.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the hotel or pick up supplies from the local Samkaup-Strax convenience store in town.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from supermarket supplies — bread, skyr, cheese, and Icelandic lamb pâté are affordable and filling.
meals.dinner: Kaffi Rauðka again or self-catered dinner at the hotel if kitchen facilities are available — pasta or rice dishes keep costs low.

day_by_day.notes: The Herring Era Museum may have limited winter hours — call ahead or check online. Avalanche risk is real in Siglufjörður in winter; always check forecasts at vedur.is before hiking above town.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south along Route 76 to explore the Tröllaskagi Peninsula (Troll Peninsula). Stop at the small village of Hofsós, known for its stunning infinity-style geothermal pool overlooking the fjord — one of Iceland's most scenic and affordable hot spring pools. Soak and warm up while taking in the dramatic winter landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving the scenic coastal road, stopping at viewpoints over Skagafjörður. Visit the small town of Sauðárkrókur if time allows — it has a supermarket (Krónan) for restocking supplies. Explore the flat farmland and mountain scenery of the Skagafjörður valley.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður before dark (around 15:30-16:00). Rest and warm up. After dinner, head out for another Northern Lights watch — the skies above the fjord are spectacular on clear nights.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel — oats, skyr, and fruit are budget-friendly and energising.
meals.lunch: Hot dog from a petrol station in Sauðárkrókur — the classic Icelandic budget meal (pylsur), typically under 500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Self-catered — stock up at Krónan in Sauðárkrókur and cook a simple meal back at the hotel.

day_by_day.notes: Hofsós swimming pool is one of Iceland's hidden gems and very affordable. Drive carefully on Route 76 in winter — ice and snow are common. Total driving distance for the day is approximately 120-150 km round trip.

day_by_day.morning: Drive west through the Héðinsfjörður tunnel and continue to Ólafsfjörður, a small fishing village in the next fjord. Walk around the harbour and explore the quiet streets. The drive through the mountain tunnels connecting the fjords is itself an experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Akureyri, Iceland's second-largest city, approximately 1 hour south of Siglufjörður. Explore the compact city centre — visit the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church (free entry), stroll the pedestrian shopping street Hafnarstræti, and browse the local shops. Visit the Akureyri Botanical Garden (free, though limited in winter).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður before conditions deteriorate. Alternatively, if roads are good, spend the evening in Akureyri and return the next morning — check road conditions at road.is.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel.
meals.lunch: Akureyri has a Bonus supermarket — grab supplies or try a budget lunch at Bautinn restaurant, known for affordable traditional Icelandic meals.
meals.dinner: If back in Siglufjörður, self-catered. If staying in Akureyri, try Strikið or a local pizza place for budget evening dining.

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri is the main service hub for the region — stock up on any supplies, medications, or gear you need. Bonus supermarket in Akureyri is the cheapest grocery option in the area. Check road.is before any drive in January.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Lake Mývatn area (approximately 1 hour east of Akureyri on Route 1). Start with the Mývatn Nature Baths — a geothermal lagoon similar to the Blue Lagoon but far less crowded and more affordable. Soak in the milky blue mineral-rich waters surrounded by volcanic landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Mývatn volcanic landscape: walk around the Skútustaðagígar pseudocraters (free), visit Dimmuborgir lava formations (free walking area), and see the Hverfjall tephra crater from the road. The otherworldly landscape is stunning even under winter snow.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward Siglufjörður via Akureyri. The drive back offers excellent Northern Lights viewing opportunities — pull over safely on the roadside if the aurora appears. Arrive back at hotel by 21:00-22:00.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast before departure.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Mývatn — bring a thermos of hot coffee or tea.
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at hotel on return.

day_by_day.notes: Mývatn Nature Baths entry is around 5,500-6,500 ISK — book online in advance for slight discount. Total driving distance approximately 200 km round trip from Siglufjörður. Start early to maximise the limited daylight hours. Dress in layers — it can be bitterly cold at Mývatn in January.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day in Siglufjörður. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely morning. Walk along the harbour in the morning light (sunrise around 11:00 in January). Visit the small local swimming pool (sundlaug) in Siglufjörður — geothermally heated, very affordable, and a great way to warm up and mingle with locals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Folk Music Centre (Þórbergssetur) in Siglufjörður if open — it celebrates Icelandic folk music traditions. Alternatively, spend the afternoon reading, journaling, or planning the rest of the trip from the warmth of the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights watch from the hotel or a dark spot near the fjord. January is statistically one of the best months for aurora activity in Iceland. Set an alarm for midnight if the forecast shows high KP index.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely self-catered breakfast — try Icelandic skyr with honey and granola.
meals.lunch: Kaffi Rauðka for a warming bowl of soup and bread.
meals.dinner: Self-catered — try cooking a traditional Icelandic lamb stew (kjötsúpa) using ingredients from the local store.

day_by_day.notes: The local swimming pool (sundlaug) is a cornerstone of Icelandic community life and typically costs only 800-1,000 ISK. This is a great budget activity and cultural experience. Use this rest day to do laundry if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east on Route 1 toward the Goðafoss waterfall (approximately 1.5 hours from Siglufjörður via Akureyri). Goðafoss — the Waterfall of the Gods — is one of Iceland's most iconic and accessible waterfalls. In January it may be partially frozen, creating a spectacular ice and water display. Entry is free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to Húsavík, Iceland's whale watching capital (approximately 30 minutes from Goðafoss). In January, whale watching tours are not operating, but the town itself is charming. Visit the Húsavík Whale Museum (Hvalasafnið) for an affordable and fascinating look at North Atlantic whale species.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður via Akureyri. The long drive back offers more aurora watching opportunities. Arrive home by 21:00.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast before departure.
meals.lunch: Húsavík has a Samkaup supermarket — grab supplies for a packed lunch or try the harbour-side Gamli Baukur restaurant for affordable fish and chips.
meals.dinner: Self-catered on return to hotel.

day_by_day.notes: Goðafoss is free and accessible year-round — the viewing platforms can be icy so wear crampons or ice grips (meðferðarís) on your boots. Total driving distance approximately 250 km round trip. Check road.is before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south from Siglufjörður toward the Skagafjörður region. Visit Glaumbær turf farm museum (Byggðasafnið á Glaumbaer) — a beautifully preserved 18th-century turf farmhouse complex. Winter hours may be limited but the exterior is always accessible and photogenic under snow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Skagafjörður valley — known as Iceland's horse country. Even in January you may spot Icelandic horses in the snowy fields. Drive to the coast for views across the fjord to the islands of Drangey and Málmey. Drangey is famous in the Grettis Saga.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður. Evening aurora watch — by now you'll know the best local spots for dark skies. Check the forecast and set an alarm if conditions look promising after midnight.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch in the car — thermos of soup is ideal for cold January days.
meals.dinner: Kaffi Rauðka for a warm meal and local atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: Glaumbær museum may have very limited or no winter hours — check ahead at glaumbaer.is. The turf farm exterior is always worth seeing even if the interior is closed. Skagafjörður is one of Iceland's most scenic and undervisited regions.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Akureyri for a more thorough exploration of the city. Visit the Akureyri Museum (Minjasafnið á Akureyri) for local history and culture at a modest entry fee. Walk up to Akureyrarkirkja church for panoramic views over the fjord.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Akureyri's affordable cultural offerings: the Christmas Garden (Jólahúsið) is open year-round and free to browse. Walk along the fjord waterfront. Visit the Lystigarðurinn botanical garden (free, though dormant in winter). Browse the second-hand shops on Hafnarstræti for budget souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Akureyri before returning to Siglufjörður. The drive back at night offers aurora watching opportunities — the road north of Akureyri is particularly dark and scenic.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast before departure.
meals.lunch: Akureyri Bonus supermarket picnic — fresh bread, smoked lamb, and Icelandic dairy products.
meals.dinner: Strikið restaurant in Akureyri offers good value set menus, or try Bautinn for classic Icelandic dishes at mid-range prices.

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri is the best place to stock up on any supplies for the remainder of the trip. The Bonus supermarket is significantly cheaper than convenience stores in Siglufjörður. Consider buying a local SIM card or topping up data here if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Full day dedicated to Northern Lights photography and aurora chasing. Sleep in after a late-night aurora watch. In the morning, research the evening forecast on vedur.is and plan your viewing location. Walk to the Siglufjörður lighthouse area for a morning stroll along the fjord.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to a high vantage point above Siglufjörður (weather and road conditions permitting) for panoramic views of the fjord and surrounding mountains. The snow-covered landscape in the low winter light is extraordinarily beautiful. Practice long-exposure photography if you have a camera and tripod.
day_by_day.evening: Dedicated Northern Lights watch evening. Drive out of town to minimise light pollution — the road toward the Héðinsfjörður tunnel offers dark skies and dramatic mountain backdrops. Stay out until midnight or later if the aurora is active.

meals.breakfast: Late self-catered breakfast — eggs, toast, and Icelandic butter.
meals.lunch: Light self-catered lunch to save energy for the evening.
meals.dinner: Early self-catered dinner before the aurora watch — something warm and hearty like lamb soup.

day_by_day.notes: The best aurora viewing requires: clear skies (check vedur.is), KP index of 3 or higher, and complete darkness. January in northern Iceland (66°N latitude) is prime aurora territory. Dress in your absolute warmest layers for extended outdoor viewing — temperatures can drop to -10°C or below with wind chill.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the scenic Tröllaskagi Peninsula route in the opposite direction — head south on Route 82 toward Varmahlíð and then loop back via Route 75 along the western side of the peninsula. This circular route passes through dramatic mountain and fjord scenery rarely visited by tourists.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the Reykir geothermal area near Varmahlíð — there is a small public swimming pool fed by natural hot springs. Soak and relax. The area around Varmahlíð also has good views of the Héraðsvatn river valley.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður via the scenic coastal road. Final evening aurora watch from the harbour — by now you'll have identified the best local spots. Reflect on the journey so far.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at a scenic viewpoint on the Tröllaskagi Peninsula.
meals.dinner: Kaffi Rauðka — treat yourself to a slightly more indulgent meal as the trip nears its end.

day_by_day.notes: Route 82 and 75 can be challenging in winter — check road.is before departure. The Tröllaskagi Peninsula is one of Iceland's most dramatic and underexplored regions. Total driving distance approximately 180-200 km.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day in Siglufjörður. Revisit your favourite spots in town — the harbour, the Herring Era Museum area, the hillside viewpoints. Take time to photograph the town in the soft winter light. Visit the local swimming pool one last time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pack and organise luggage for departure the next day. Take a final walk along the fjord. Buy any last-minute local souvenirs — dried fish (harðfiskur), Icelandic wool products, or local jams from the Samkaup store are affordable and authentic gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Final Northern Lights watch in Siglufjörður. Head to the darkest spot you've found during the trip. Savour the experience of being in one of the world's best aurora viewing locations. Celebrate the trip with a local Icelandic beer (Víking or Egill) at Kaffi Rauðka.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — use up remaining food supplies.
meals.lunch: Light self-catered lunch.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Kaffi Rauðka — the fish of the day or lamb dish is recommended.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time at Hotel Siglunes — confirm with reception. Prepare for an early departure the next morning. Ensure the car is fuelled up. Check road.is for conditions on the route south to Keflavik.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure from Siglufjörður. The drive to Keflavik International Airport takes approximately 5-6 hours depending on road conditions and stops. Depart by 06:00-07:00 to allow ample time. Drive south through Akureyri, then west along Route 1 (the Ring Road) toward Reykjavik and Keflavik.
day_by_day.afternoon: If time allows before your flight, stop at a geothermal pool along the way — the Laugarvatn Fontana or the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir are affordable options near the Ring Road. Alternatively, stop at a viewpoint over the Hvalfjörður fjord or the lava fields near Reykjanes.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport with plenty of time before departure. Return the rental car if applicable. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days in northern Iceland — the Northern Lights, the hot springs, the dramatic fjords, and the warmth of Icelandic hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Very early self-catered breakfast before departure — prepare the night before.
meals.lunch: Petrol station stop along Route 1 — hot dog (pylsur) and coffee is the classic Icelandic road trip meal.
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Keflavik — budget options available in the departure hall.

day_by_day.notes: Allow extra time for winter driving conditions — ice, snow, and reduced visibility are common in January. Check road.is before departure. The Flybus from Reykjavik BSI to Keflavik airport runs regularly and is cheaper than a taxi. Keep warm layers accessible in your hand luggage for the journey home.

trip_options.title: Classic Iceland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavik International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs, collect luggage, and pick up pre-booked rental car (4WD essential for winter Iceland). Grab a coffee and light breakfast at the airport café before beginning the long drive north to Siglufjörður (approx. 5–6 hours via Route 1 and Tunnel). Drive through the Hvalfjörður tunnel and along the dramatic Snæfellsnes peninsula coastline in the early morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the scenic drive north through Borgarnes and Blönduós. Stop at a roadside petrol station in Blönduós for a warm meal and fuel. Admire the stark winter landscape of the Icelandic highlands and frozen rivers along Route 1. Cross the Héðinsfjörður tunnel into Siglufjörður in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to Hotel Siglunes in Lækjargata 10, Siglufjörður. Freshen up and take a short stroll around the charming, quiet fishing village. Have dinner at the hotel restaurant or nearby Hannes Boy restaurant, known for fresh local fish and lamb dishes. Early night to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Airport café at Keflavik — coffee, skyr yogurt, and pastry (~1,500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Roadside stop in Blönduós — soup of the day and bread at a petrol station café (~2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Hannes Boy restaurant in Siglufjörður — pan-fried Arctic char with roasted vegetables (~4,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Road conditions in January can be severe — check road.is before and during the drive. The Héðinsfjörður tunnel closes occasionally in storms. Allow extra travel time. Sunset is around 16:00 in January, so most of the drive will be in darkness after Blönduós.

day_by_day.morning: After a well-deserved rest, enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. Visit the Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) in Siglufjörður, one of Iceland's finest regional museums, documenting the town's booming herring fishing history with fascinating exhibits and restored boats. Open from 10:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Siglufjörður fjord on foot — walk along the harbour waterfront and admire the colourful wooden houses dusted with snow. Drive the short distance to Hofsós village (approx. 40 min south) to see the stunning infinity geothermal pool perched above the fjord — a hidden gem with panoramic views of Skagafjörður.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður for dinner. Keep eyes on the northern lights forecast (vedur.is) — if aurora activity is predicted (KP index 3+), head to the dark hillside above town after dinner for Northern Lights viewing. The fjord's natural darkness and mountain backdrop make it an excellent spot.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes breakfast buffet — eggs, skyr, rye bread, smoked salmon (~included or ~2,500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Café Rauðka in Siglufjörður — homemade soup and Icelandic lamb sandwich (~2,200 ISK)
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes restaurant — slow-cooked lamb shank with root vegetables and Icelandic potatoes (~5,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Hofsós infinity pool is open year-round and costs around 1,000 ISK entry. Bring a swimsuit and towel. The drive to Hofsós on Route 76 is scenic but can be icy — drive carefully. Download the Vedur app for real-time aurora forecasts.

day_by_day.morning: Drive west along the Tröllaskagi peninsula (Trolls' Peninsula) on Route 76 — one of Iceland's most dramatic coastal roads with towering mountains plunging into the sea. Stop at Dalvík village (approx. 1 hour from Siglufjörður) and visit the quirky Byggðasafnið Hvoll folk museum, which includes a display on the world's tallest man.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Akureyri, Iceland's second-largest city (approx. 40 min from Dalvík). Explore the charming town centre — visit the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church perched on the hill, browse the Akureyri Art Museum, and stroll the pedestrian shopping street Hafnarstræti. Enjoy the famous heart-shaped traffic lights unique to Akureyri.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Akureyri before returning to Siglufjörður. On the return drive, stop at a dark viewpoint above the fjord for Northern Lights watching if conditions are favourable.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes breakfast buffet
meals.lunch: Bautinn Restaurant in Akureyri — traditional Icelandic meat soup and fresh bread (~2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Strikið Restaurant in Akureyri — pan-seared cod with herb butter and seasonal vegetables (~5,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri is approximately 1.5 hours from Siglufjörður via the Ólafsfjörður and Vaðlaheiðargöng tunnels. The tunnel toll is around 1,500 ISK each way. Akureyri has excellent supermarkets (Krónan, Nettó) — stock up on snacks and supplies for the week.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Lake Mývatn area (approx. 1.5 hours east of Akureyri on Route 1). Begin at the Námaskarð geothermal area (Hverir) — a surreal, otherworldly landscape of bubbling mud pools, steaming fumaroles, and sulphur-stained earth. Walk the marked paths carefully as the ground is unstable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mývatn Nature Baths — Iceland's lesser-known but equally spectacular geothermal lagoon with stunning views over the volcanic landscape. Soak in the mineral-rich, silica-blue waters at a comfortable 36–40°C. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon and equally rejuvenating. Entry approx. 6,500 ISK.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the bizarre Dimmuborgir lava formations (the 'Dark Castles') near Lake Mývatn — a labyrinth of twisted lava pillars and arches formed 2,300 years ago. Then drive back toward Siglufjörður, watching for Northern Lights on the open road. Dinner at the hotel upon return.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes breakfast buffet
meals.lunch: Vogafjós Farm Restaurant at Mývatn — famous for geothermally baked rye bread with smoked trout and local cheese (~3,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes restaurant — grilled lamb fillet with wild mushroom sauce (~5,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Mývatn Nature Baths require advance booking in winter — book online at myvatnnaturebaths.is. Bring a swimsuit and towel. The Námaskarð area can be slippery with ice — wear sturdy boots. Total driving for the day is approximately 3.5–4 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning in Siglufjörður — sleep in and enjoy a slow breakfast. Visit the local swimming pool (Sundlaug Siglufjarðar) — a beloved community geothermal pool with hot tubs, perfect for warming up on a cold January morning. Entry approx. 1,000 ISK.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Sauðárkrókur (approx. 1 hour south on Route 76) — the largest town in Skagafjörður. Visit the Skagafjörður Heritage Museum to learn about the region's Viking and horse-breeding heritage. Skagafjörður is famous for Icelandic horses — look for herds in the snowy fields along the road.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting Tour — book a guided evening tour departing from Akureyri or Siglufjörður area. A local guide will drive you to optimal dark-sky locations based on real-time aurora forecasts, maximising your chances of seeing the aurora borealis dance across the sky. Tours typically run 21:00–00:00.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes breakfast buffet
meals.lunch: Kaffi Krókur in Sauðárkrókur — homemade fish soup and Icelandic flatbread (~2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes restaurant — beef stew with root vegetables and fresh bread (~4,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Northern Lights tours from the Akureyri area cost approximately 9,000–12,000 ISK per person. Book in advance through operators like Arctic Adventures or local Akureyri tour companies. Dress in extreme warmth — multiple layers, waterproof outer shell, hat, gloves, and thermal boots are essential.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south on Route 1 toward the Snæfellsnes Peninsula (approx. 3.5 hours). Stop at Glaumbær turf farm museum near Varmahlíð — a beautifully preserved 18th-century turf farmhouse complex, one of Iceland's best examples of traditional architecture. Open limited hours in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Snæfellsnes Peninsula and visit Snæfellsjökull National Park. Drive the peninsula's southern coast, stopping at the dramatic Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach with its rusting shipwreck remains and sea stacks. Walk to the Gatklettur arch rock formation nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to a guesthouse in Grundarfjörður or Stykkishólmur for the night (pre-booked mid-range accommodation, approx. 15,000–20,000 ISK). Dinner in town and aurora watching from the harbour.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes breakfast buffet (early departure)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from hotel or petrol station stop — skyr, fruit, and a warm pastry
meals.dinner: Narfeyrarstofa Restaurant in Stykkishólmur — pan-fried scallops and local lamb (~5,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: This is a travel-heavy day — start early (by 08:00) to make the most of the limited daylight hours (roughly 09:30–16:00). Snæfellsnes roads can be icy and windy in January. The Snæfellsjökull glacier is often cloud-covered but still dramatic. Check road.is before departing.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the northern coast of Snæfellsnes Peninsula. Visit Kirkjufell mountain — Iceland's most photographed mountain — and the adjacent Kirkjufellsfoss waterfall near Grundarfjörður. The mountain is particularly magical in winter with snow and ice. Walk the short path to the waterfall viewpoint.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Stykkishólmur and explore the charming harbour town. Visit the Norwegian House (Norska Húsið) museum and climb to the lighthouse on the rocky island of Súgandisey for panoramic views of the fjord and surrounding islands. Browse the small local shops.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Reykjavik (approx. 2 hours) and check in to a mid-range hotel in Reykjavik (pre-booked, approx. 18,000–25,000 ISK per night). Dinner in Reykjavik's vibrant restaurant scene.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or Grundarfjörður bakery — fresh pastries and coffee (~1,500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Sjávarpakkhúsið in Stykkishólmur — fresh fish and chips with local beer (~3,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Messinn Restaurant in Reykjavik — signature cast-iron pan of fresh Icelandic fish (~5,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Kirkjufell is best photographed at dawn or dusk — the golden hour light on the snow-covered peak is spectacular. The path to Kirkjufellsfoss can be icy; use microspikes if available. Reykjavik hotel options: Centerhotel Þingholt, Hotel Borg, or similar mid-range properties.

day_by_day.morning: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa — pre-booked visit (essential in winter). Drive 45 minutes from Reykjavik to the iconic milky-blue geothermal lagoon near Grindavík. Soak in the mineral-rich 37–39°C waters, enjoy the silica mud mask stations, and relax in the steam rooms. Book the Comfort package (approx. 14,000 ISK) which includes towel, silica mask, and algae mask.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Reykjavik and explore the city. Visit Hallgrímskirkja church and take the elevator to the top for panoramic city views. Walk down Skólavörðustígur street browsing local design shops and galleries. Visit the Harpa Concert Hall on the waterfront — the glass facade is stunning in winter light.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Reykjavik's famous nightlife and restaurant scene on Laugavegur street. Enjoy dinner at a mid-range restaurant before an evening stroll through the illuminated city centre.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Reykjavik
meals.lunch: Blue Lagoon LAVA Restaurant — light lunch of Icelandic seafood soup and bread (~4,000 ISK) or pack a lunch to eat after the lagoon
meals.dinner: Grillmarkaðurinn (The Grill Market) in Reykjavik — Icelandic lamb burger with local cheese and fries (~5,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Blue Lagoon MUST be booked well in advance — visit bluelagoon.com. Arrive at your booked time slot. The lagoon is open from 08:00 in winter. Avoid bringing jewellery into the water as the minerals can damage metals. The drive from Reykjavik passes through dramatic lava fields.

day_by_day.morning: Golden Circle day trip from Reykjavik. Start at Þingvellir National Park (UNESCO World Heritage Site) — walk the Almannagjá rift valley between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates. The site is also Iceland's ancient parliament grounds. Dress warmly as the open plain is very exposed.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Geysir geothermal area — watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting boiling water 20–30 metres into the air. Then drive to Gullfoss waterfall — Iceland's most powerful waterfall, partially frozen in January with spectacular ice formations. The thundering water and ice create an unforgettable scene.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik. Stop at the Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring in Flúðir on the return route (approx. 1 hour from Gullfoss) — Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a naturally heated geothermal pool surrounded by bubbling hot springs and a small geyser. Entry approx. 3,500 ISK. Return to Reykjavik for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Reykjavik
meals.lunch: Geysir Centre café — lamb soup and Icelandic rye bread (~2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Café Loki in Reykjavik — traditional Icelandic hákarl tasting plate, lamb soup, and skyr dessert (~4,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Golden Circle is approximately 300 km round trip from Reykjavik. Start early (08:30) to maximise daylight. The Secret Lagoon in Flúðir is a wonderful, less-commercialised alternative to the Blue Lagoon — book at secretlagoon.is. Bring a swimsuit and towel.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure at Þingvellir National Park — a once-in-a-lifetime experience snorkelling between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water with visibility up to 100 metres. The water is a constant 2–4°C so dry suits are provided. Tours depart around 09:00. Book with DIVE.IS or Arctic Adventures (approx. 25,000–30,000 ISK for snorkelling).
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Silfra experience, warm up with hot chocolate and dry off. Drive back toward Reykjavik and visit the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) in the city centre — a fascinating underground museum built around the remains of a Viking longhouse from 871 AD.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting Tour from Reykjavik — join a guided evening minibus tour that chases the aurora away from city light pollution. Guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots. Tours run approximately 21:00–00:00 (approx. 9,000–11,000 ISK).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Reykjavik (early, before 08:00 departure)
meals.lunch: Þingvellir National Park visitor centre café — warm soup and sandwich (~2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) in Reykjavik — famous lobster soup and grilled fish skewers (~3,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Silfra snorkelling requires a minimum chest size and swimming ability — check requirements when booking. You cannot dive/snorkel if you have certain medical conditions. The dry suit keeps you dry but the cold water on your face is intense — prepare mentally. This is one of Iceland's most unique experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the South Coast from Reykjavik. First stop: Seljalandsfoss waterfall (approx. 2 hours east on Route 1) — a stunning 60-metre waterfall with a path that goes behind the curtain of water. In January the path may be icy and partially closed — check conditions. Nearby Gljúfrabúi hidden waterfall is also worth the short scramble.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to Skógafoss waterfall — one of Iceland's largest and most dramatic waterfalls, often with ice formations at the base in January. Climb the 370 steps to the top for panoramic views of the South Coast. Then drive to the black sand beach at Reynisfjara near Vík — dramatic basalt columns, sea caves, and powerful Atlantic waves. NEVER turn your back on the ocean here — sneaker waves are deadly.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back west toward Reykjavik (approx. 2.5 hours). Stop at Skaftá Bistro or a roadside restaurant for dinner. Watch for Northern Lights on the open South Coast road — the flat terrain and minimal light pollution make it excellent for aurora viewing.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Reykjavik (early departure by 07:30)
meals.lunch: Skógar Museum café near Skógafoss — lamb soup and fresh bread (~2,200 ISK)
meals.dinner: Halldórskaffi in Hvolsvöllur on the return drive — traditional Icelandic meat soup and pan-fried fish (~4,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: This is a long day (approx. 400 km round trip) — start very early. Reynisfjara beach is extremely dangerous; stay well back from the waterline and watch the waves constantly. The South Coast road (Route 1) is generally well-maintained but can have black ice. Microspikes are useful at the waterfalls.

day_by_day.morning: Skaftafell Glacier Hike on Vatnajökull — this requires an early start and a long drive (approx. 3.5 hours from Reykjavik to Skaftafell). Join a guided glacier hike on Svínafellsjökull glacier outlet (part of Vatnajökull, Europe's largest glacier). Strap on crampons and explore stunning ice formations, crevasses, and blue ice caves with an expert guide. Tours depart around 11:00 from the Skaftafell visitor centre (approx. 12,000–15,000 ISK).
day_by_day.afternoon: After the glacier hike, visit the nearby Svartifoss waterfall in Skaftafell — a beautiful black basalt column waterfall (approx. 1.5 km hike each way). If time permits, drive to the Jökulsárlón glacier lagoon (approx. 45 min further east) — watch icebergs calve from the glacier and float in the lagoon, then walk to Diamond Beach where ice chunks wash up on black sand.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the long drive back to Reykjavik (approx. 4 hours). Stop for dinner in Kirkjubæjarklaustur — a small village with a good restaurant. Watch for Northern Lights on the vast, dark South Coast road.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Reykjavik (very early, 06:30)
meals.lunch: Skaftafell visitor centre café — hot soup and sandwich after the glacier hike (~2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Systrakaffi in Kirkjubæjarklaustur — lamb stew and Icelandic flatbread (~4,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: This is the longest and most demanding day of the trip — approximately 700 km round trip. Consider staying overnight in Kirkjubæjarklaustur or near Jökulsárlón to break the journey (pre-book if so). The glacier hike requires moderate fitness. All equipment (crampons, harness, helmet) is provided by the guide company. Book with Icelandic Mountain Guides or Local Guide.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Reykjavik — leisurely breakfast and last-minute souvenir shopping on Laugavegur and Skólavörðustígur streets. Visit the Kolaportið flea market (open weekends) for local crafts, vintage items, and traditional Icelandic food stalls including hákarl (fermented shark) and dried fish. Visit the National Museum of Iceland for a final dose of Icelandic history and culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Perlan museum on Öskjuhlíð hill — a stunning glass dome building with a 360° observation deck offering panoramic views of Reykjavik and the surrounding mountains and sea. Inside, explore the excellent 'Wonders of Iceland' exhibition including a real ice cave tunnel. Entry approx. 4,500 ISK.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Reykjavik — celebrate the end of an incredible Iceland adventure. Head to the airport for any late departures, or rest at the hotel for an early morning flight. Take one last look at the sky for a farewell aurora display.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Reykjavik — enjoy a full Icelandic spread one last time
meals.lunch: Bergsson Mathús in Reykjavik — fresh salads, open-faced sandwiches, and excellent coffee (~2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Fiskmarkaðurinn (The Fish Market) in Reykjavik — sushi-style Icelandic seafood tasting menu (~7,000 ISK) — a special farewell splurge

day_by_day.notes: Return the rental car with a full tank of petrol — fuel up before reaching the airport. Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for car return, shuttle, and check-in. Duty-free at Keflavik airport is excellent for Icelandic spirits (Brennivín), chocolate, and skincare products. The Blue Lagoon silica products make great gifts.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunting Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided evening tour away from Reykjavik's light pollution to witness the aurora borealis dancing across the sky. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind this natural phenomenon while capturing stunning photographs.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and swim-up bars while surrounded by dramatic lava fields. Book the Comfort package for access to the main lagoon, towel rental, and one silica mud mask.

experiences.name: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure
experiences.description: Snorkel or dive between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water with visibility up to 100 meters. The surreal blue and green hues of the water make this one of the most unique natural experiences on Earth, guided by certified instructors.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring
experiences.description: Relax in Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a naturally heated geothermal pool surrounded by bubbling hot springs and a small geyser that erupts every few minutes. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic experience offers a peaceful soak amid stunning Icelandic countryside.

experiences.name: Skaftafell Glacier Hike on Vatnajökull
experiences.description: Strap on crampons and hike across Europe's largest glacier with an expert guide. Explore stunning ice formations, deep blue crevasses, and ash layers from ancient volcanic eruptions. The hike offers breathtaking panoramic views of the surrounding black sand plains and mountain peaks.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavík International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage, then transfer via pre-arranged luxury private car service northward toward Siglufjörður (approximately 4.5–5 hour scenic drive). Stop at a roadside viewpoint near Borgarnes to stretch and take in the dramatic winter landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the scenic drive through the Tröllaskagi peninsula, passing through Akureyri and winding along the fjord roads. Arrive at Hotel Siglunes in Siglufjörður by early afternoon. Check in, unpack, and settle into your premium room overlooking the fjord. Take a gentle self-guided stroll through the charming, snow-dusted streets of Siglufjörður — Iceland's northernmost town — visiting the iconic red harbour and colourful wooden houses.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and recover from the overnight flight. Head to the hotel's intimate dining room for a relaxed welcome dinner featuring locally sourced Icelandic ingredients. Afterwards, step outside or onto your balcony to scan the sky for early northern lights activity — Siglufjörður's minimal light pollution makes it an exceptional aurora-viewing location.

meals.breakfast: Light refreshments and coffee at Keflavík Airport's premium lounge or en route at a quality café in Borgarnes such as Hyrnan Café
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet picnic box arranged by your private driver, or a warm stop at Bautinn Restaurant in Akureyri for traditional Icelandic lamb soup
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes restaurant — indulge in pan-seared Arctic char with dill butter, locally foraged mushroom risotto, and Icelandic skyr panna cotta for dessert, paired with a curated Icelandic craft beer or imported wine

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange your luxury private airport transfer well in advance. The drive from Keflavík to Siglufjörður is long but spectacular — consider hiring a driver so you can rest. Pack warm layers immediately accessible in your carry-on as temperatures will be around 0–5°C upon arrival. Download the Icelandic Met Office aurora forecast app (vedur.is) before landing.

day_by_day.morning: After a restorative night's sleep, enjoy a leisurely late breakfast at the hotel. Then visit the award-winning Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) — one of Iceland's finest regional museums — which tells the fascinating story of Siglufjörður's herring boom era through immersive exhibits and restored period buildings. The museum is a short walk from the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Embark on a guided snowshoe or winter hiking excursion into the mountains surrounding Siglufjörður with a local expert guide. The dramatic fjord scenery, snow-covered peaks, and near-total silence create an otherworldly premium nature experience. Return to the hotel for a warm soak in the hotel's hot tub overlooking the fjord.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting Tour — join a small-group guided aurora tour departing from Siglufjörður. Your expert guide will drive to optimal dark-sky locations in the surrounding fjords and mountains, monitoring cloud cover and solar activity in real time. Enjoy hot chocolate and Icelandic pastries while waiting for the aurora to dance overhead.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at Hotel Siglunes — skyr with berries, smoked salmon on rye, scrambled eggs, Icelandic cheeses, and freshly baked bread
meals.lunch: Warm lunch at Kaffi Rauðka, Siglufjörður's beloved local café — homemade lamb stew, fresh-baked cinnamon rolls, and Icelandic coffee
meals.dinner: Return to Hotel Siglunes for a premium three-course dinner — begin with langoustine bisque, followed by slow-roasted reindeer with root vegetable purée and lingonberry jus, finishing with warm chocolate lava cake and Icelandic ice cream

day_by_day.notes: The Northern Lights are never guaranteed, but January in Siglufjörður offers some of Iceland's best aurora conditions due to long dark nights (sunrise ~11:00, sunset ~15:30) and low light pollution. Dress in thermal base layers, mid-layers, and a windproof outer shell. Hand warmers are highly recommended. Book the aurora tour through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to the Siglufjörður Ski Resort (Skíðasvæðið á Skarðshlíð) — one of Iceland's most scenic and underrated ski areas, located just minutes from the hotel. Enjoy a private ski or snowboard lesson with a local instructor, or simply ride the lifts for panoramic views of the fjord below. Equipment rental available on-site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or arrange a private transfer along the stunning Tröllaskagi peninsula to the nearby village of Hofsós, home to one of Iceland's most dramatically situated geothermal swimming pools — the Hofsós Infinity Pool. Perched on a cliff edge overlooking the fjord, this premium hot spring experience feels like bathing at the edge of the world. Soak for 1–2 hours in the naturally heated waters.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður for a quiet evening. Visit the local liquor store to pick up a bottle of Brennivín (Icelandic schnapps) or a premium Icelandic gin for a nightcap. Dine at the hotel and spend the post-dinner hours aurora watching from the harbour — bring a tripod if you enjoy astrophotography.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — freshly baked pastries, Icelandic yoghurt, smoked lamb, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the ski resort's mountain café — hearty lamb soup, open-faced sandwiches, and hot drinks
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes — pan-fried cod with brown butter and capers, roasted root vegetables, and a selection from the hotel's curated wine list

day_by_day.notes: Hofsós is approximately 45 minutes south of Siglufjörður. The infinity pool is open year-round but check seasonal hours in advance. January daylight is extremely limited (roughly 11:00–15:30), so plan outdoor activities to maximise the brief window of natural light. The ski resort is best visited in the morning when snow conditions are freshest.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Siglufjörður after breakfast on a scenic drive to Akureyri — Iceland's 'Capital of the North' (approximately 1 hour). Explore the charming town centre: visit the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church perched dramatically above the town, browse the boutique shops along Hafnarstræti, and stop at the Akureyri Art Museum for a curated exhibition of Icelandic contemporary art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Akureyri Botanical Garden (Lystigarðurinn) — the world's northernmost botanical garden — which in winter transforms into a serene snow-covered landscape. Then head to the Geosea Geothermal Sea Baths in nearby Húsavík (approximately 1 hour from Akureyri) — a luxury clifftop geothermal spa with infinity pools overlooking Skjálfandi Bay, where you may spot humpback whales even in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Dine in Akureyri at one of Iceland's finest regional restaurants before returning to Siglufjörður. Alternatively, if the aurora forecast is strong, ask your driver to stop at a dark-sky location en route back for impromptu northern lights viewing.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes farewell breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Rub23 Restaurant in Akureyri — one of Iceland's most celebrated restaurants outside Reykjavík, known for exceptional sushi and Icelandic seafood fusion
meals.dinner: Strikið Restaurant in Akureyri — rooftop dining with panoramic fjord views, featuring premium Icelandic lamb, fresh seafood, and an extensive wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Geosea Geothermal Sea Baths in Húsavík is a 90-minute drive from Akureyri — factor this into your day's timing given limited daylight. Book Geosea and dinner reservations well in advance. Road conditions in January can be challenging; ensure your private driver has a 4WD vehicle with winter tyres. Check road.is for live conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Siglufjörður after an early breakfast and begin the scenic drive south toward the Golden Circle region (approximately 5–6 hours). Stop at Goðafoss — the 'Waterfall of the Gods' — one of Iceland's most spectacular waterfalls, dramatically framed by ice and snow in January. Spend 30–45 minutes photographing and exploring the viewpoints.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue south and visit Geysir Geothermal Area in the Haukadalur valley — home to the famous Strokkur geyser, which erupts every 5–10 minutes shooting boiling water up to 40 metres into the frigid air. The contrast of steam, snow, and erupting water is extraordinary in winter. Then visit the majestic Gullfoss waterfall, partially frozen in January, creating a breathtaking ice sculpture landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to your luxury accommodation in the Golden Circle area (recommend Hótel Geysir or Frost and Fire Hotel in Flúðir). Enjoy a premium dinner at the hotel restaurant and spend the evening in the hotel's private outdoor geothermal hot tubs, watching for northern lights above the steam.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Hotel Siglunes before departure
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch box from the hotel, enjoyed at Goðafoss viewpoint or en route
meals.dinner: Hótel Geysir Restaurant or Frost and Fire Hotel dining room — locally sourced Icelandic lamb, fresh trout from the Hvítá river, and seasonal vegetables, paired with Icelandic craft beer

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day — approximately 5–6 hours total. Depart by 08:00 to make the most of the limited daylight window. The Golden Circle is one of Iceland's most visited routes but in January crowds are minimal. Frost and Fire Hotel in Flúðir has exceptional private geothermal pools — highly recommended for overnight stay. Book well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Þingvellir National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of Iceland's most historically and geologically significant locations. Walk along the Almannagjá rift valley, where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates are visibly pulling apart. In January, the park is blanketed in snow and almost entirely crowd-free, creating an ethereal premium experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring in Flúðir — Iceland's oldest swimming pool, dating to 1891. Soak in the naturally heated geothermal waters (38–40°C) surrounded by bubbling hot springs, steaming vents, and a small geyser that erupts every few minutes. The winter setting, with snow on the ground and steam rising into the cold air, is magical. Enjoy the included silica mud mask and in-water relaxation.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting Tour — depart from your Golden Circle accommodation with a specialist aurora guide. The flat, open landscape of the interior highlands provides unobstructed 360-degree sky views, ideal for aurora photography. Your guide will provide professional camera settings advice and a tripod if needed.

meals.breakfast: Luxury hotel breakfast — smoked salmon eggs Benedict, Icelandic pastries, fresh fruit, and barista coffee
meals.lunch: Þingvellir National Park Visitor Centre café — warm soup, sandwiches, and hot drinks in a cosy setting
meals.dinner: Return to hotel for a premium dinner — pan-seared langoustine tails, Icelandic beef tenderloin with truffle butter, and a decadent skyr cheesecake

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon is far less commercialised than the Blue Lagoon and offers a more authentic, intimate experience. Book tickets in advance online. Þingvellir is also the location of the Silfra Fissure snorkelling experience — if you wish to combine both in one day, depart very early. Dress in full waterproof gear for Þingvellir as wind chill can be severe.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure at Þingvellir National Park — one of the world's most extraordinary underwater experiences. Don a dry suit and snorkel (or dive) between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in water of exceptional clarity (visibility up to 100 metres). The water temperature is 2–4°C but dry suits keep you warm. This is a once-in-a-lifetime premium adventure.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Silfra experience, warm up with hot chocolate and a change of clothes, then drive toward the South Coast. Stop at Kerið volcanic crater lake — a vivid red and ochre caldera filled with a striking turquoise lake, partially iced over in January. Continue to your luxury South Coast accommodation (recommend Icelandair Hotel Rangá or Deplar Farm).
day_by_day.evening: Check in to your South Coast luxury lodge. Icelandair Hotel Rangá is renowned as one of Iceland's premier northern lights viewing hotels, with dedicated aurora wake-up calls and outdoor hot tubs perfectly positioned for sky watching. Enjoy a gourmet dinner at the hotel's acclaimed restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at hotel before the Silfra tour (a full stomach is not recommended before snorkelling)
meals.lunch: Post-Silfra warm lunch at a nearby café in Selfoss — hearty lamb soup and fresh bread to restore warmth
meals.dinner: Icelandair Hotel Rangá Restaurant — celebrated for its exceptional Icelandic cuisine; try the slow-cooked lamb shank with root vegetable gratin, followed by Icelandic cheese board and local honey

day_by_day.notes: The Silfra snorkelling tour requires advance booking through a certified operator (Dive.is or Arctic Adventures). Participants must be comfortable in water — no prior diving experience needed for snorkelling. Minimum age is typically 12. The dry suit fitting takes 30–45 minutes before entering the water. Bring a change of warm clothes and thermal layers for immediately after. The experience lasts approximately 3 hours total.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Iceland's dramatic South Coast. Begin at Seljalandsfoss waterfall — in January, the falls are partially frozen and the surrounding icicles create a spectacular ice cathedral. Walk behind the curtain of water (conditions permitting in winter) for a unique perspective. Continue to the equally stunning Skógafoss waterfall, where ice formations and rainbows in the mist make for extraordinary photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the black sand beach at Reynisfjara — one of the world's most dramatic beaches, with towering basalt column formations, roaring Atlantic waves, and the iconic Reynisdrangar sea stacks rising from the ocean. Exercise extreme caution with sneaker waves. Continue to the picturesque village of Vík í Mýrdal for a brief exploration of Iceland's southernmost village.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Icelandair Hotel Rangá for a relaxing evening. Take advantage of the hotel's outdoor hot tubs under the open sky — the hotel's aurora wake-up service will alert you if the lights appear overnight. Enjoy a nightcap at the hotel bar featuring Icelandic spirits.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at Icelandair Hotel Rangá — eggs cooked to order, smoked meats, Icelandic cheeses, fresh pastries, and freshly squeezed juice
meals.lunch: Lunch at Skool Beans café in Vík — a converted double-decker bus serving excellent soups, sandwiches, and coffee in a quirky setting
meals.dinner: Hotel Rangá — premium tasting menu featuring seasonal Icelandic ingredients: reindeer carpaccio, lobster bisque, pan-seared halibut, and a dessert of warm Icelandic doughnuts (kleinar) with vanilla cream

day_by_day.notes: Reynisfjara beach is genuinely dangerous — rogue waves have claimed lives. Never turn your back on the ocean and stay well back from the waterline. In January, Seljalandsfoss walkway behind the falls may be closed due to ice — check locally. The South Coast is one of Iceland's wettest regions; waterproof gear is essential. Sunrise is approximately 11:00 and sunset around 16:00.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for the Skaftafell area within Vatnajökull National Park (approximately 2 hours east of Vík). Embark on the Skaftafell Glacier Hike on Vatnajökull — strap on crampons and harness with an expert mountain guide and hike across Europe's largest glacier. Explore stunning blue ice caves, crevasses, and glacial formations. The January light creates extraordinary blue hues inside the ice.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the glacier hike, visit the nearby Diamond Beach (Breiðamerkursandur) — where enormous chunks of glacial ice, some crystal clear and others vivid blue, wash up on the black sand beach from the adjacent Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon. Spend time at Jökulsárlón itself, where icebergs drift silently through the lagoon — a surreal and deeply moving natural spectacle.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back west toward the hotel. If time and conditions allow, stop at a dark-sky location for aurora viewing en route. Return to Icelandair Hotel Rangá for a late dinner and well-deserved rest after a physically demanding day.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Hotel Rangá before departure — packed thermos of coffee and energy snacks for the glacier hike
meals.lunch: Packed premium lunch box from the hotel, enjoyed at Skaftafell Visitor Centre or on the glacier tour
meals.dinner: Hotel Rangá — comfort dining after a long day: Icelandic beef burger with truffle fries, or a warming bowl of traditional kjötsúpa (lamb soup), followed by warm apple cake with Icelandic cream

day_by_day.notes: The glacier hike is physically demanding and requires a reasonable level of fitness. Wear sturdy waterproof hiking boots (crampons are provided by the guide). The tour operator will provide all safety equipment. Book through a certified glacier guide company such as Glacier Guides or Local Guide. The ice cave experience inside Vatnajökull is one of the world's most extraordinary natural wonders — January is peak season for blue ice cave tours. Book months in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning at Icelandair Hotel Rangá — sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast, and use the hotel's wellness facilities. Take a soak in the outdoor hot tubs in the crisp morning air, watching steam rise against the backdrop of Hekla volcano. This is a deliberate rest day to recharge after the physically intensive glacier day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Westman Islands ferry terminal at Landeyjahöfn (approximately 30 minutes from Hotel Rangá) for a day trip to Heimaey — the largest of the Westman Islands (Vestmannaeyjar). Explore the dramatic volcanic landscape shaped by the 1973 Eldfell eruption, visit the Eldheimar Museum (built around a house buried in lava), and walk the volcanic crater rim for panoramic ocean views.
day_by_day.evening: Return by ferry to the mainland and drive back to Hotel Rangá. Enjoy a premium spa treatment at the hotel (book in advance) — a traditional Icelandic hot stone massage or a volcanic mud body wrap. Dine at the hotel and retire early.

meals.breakfast: Extended luxury breakfast at Hotel Rangá — take your time and enjoy every element of the spread
meals.lunch: Lunch on Heimaey island at Einsi Kaldi Restaurant — fresh local seafood, Westman Islands puffin (seasonal), and Icelandic craft beer
meals.dinner: Hotel Rangá — lighter evening meal: smoked salmon salad, Icelandic cheese and charcuterie board, and a glass of premium Champagne to celebrate the midpoint of the trip

day_by_day.notes: The Westman Islands ferry (Herjólfur) runs year-round but can be cancelled in rough weather — check Sæferðir.is for schedules and conditions. The crossing takes approximately 35 minutes. Heimaey is a fascinating and undervisited destination that rewards curious travellers. The Eldheimar Museum is world-class. Wrap up warmly as the island is exposed to Atlantic winds.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Icelandair Hotel Rangá and drive to the Reykjanes Peninsula for the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa experience — one of the world's most iconic wellness destinations. Arrive for a premium Retreat Spa package: enjoy the signature silica mud mask, algae mask, and in-water massage. The milky-blue 38–40°C waters are rich in silica, minerals, and algae with genuine skin-healing properties.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Blue Lagoon experience — enjoy the exclusive Retreat Lounge (included in premium packages) with complimentary sparkling wine, fresh fruit, and panoramic lagoon views. Afterwards, check in to your Reykjavík luxury hotel (recommend The Retreat at Blue Lagoon Iceland for ultimate luxury, or Hotel Borg in central Reykjavík for a classic art deco experience).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Reykjavík's vibrant Laugavegur street for boutique shopping and gallery browsing. Dine at one of Reykjavík's finest restaurants for a premium Icelandic fine dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hotel Rangá before checkout
meals.lunch: LAVA Restaurant at the Blue Lagoon — dine in the lagoon itself with floating tray service, enjoying fresh Icelandic seafood and light dishes while soaking in the geothermal waters
meals.dinner: Dill Restaurant in Reykjavík — Iceland's only Michelin-starred restaurant, offering a stunning Nordic tasting menu that celebrates Icelandic ingredients through innovative, seasonal cuisine. Book months in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Blue Lagoon must be booked well in advance — premium Retreat packages sell out months ahead, especially in January. Arrive at your allocated time slot. Silica can dry hair significantly — the lagoon provides conditioner to apply before entering. Remove all jewellery before entering as silica can discolour metals. The drive from Hotel Rangá to Blue Lagoon is approximately 1.5 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Reykjavík's world-class cultural offerings. Visit Hallgrímskirkja church and take the elevator to the tower for panoramic city and mountain views. Then visit the Harpa Concert Hall — an architectural masterpiece of geometric glass panels on the harbour — and explore the National Museum of Iceland for a deep dive into Icelandic history and Viking heritage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) — built around a genuine Viking-age longhouse excavated beneath the city streets. Then take a premium whale watching tour from the Old Harbour (Elding or Special Tours) — January offers excellent chances of seeing humpback whales and white-beaked dolphins in Faxaflói Bay, with far fewer tourists than summer.
day_by_day.evening: Final Northern Lights Hunting Tour — depart from Reykjavík with a specialist aurora guide who monitors real-time solar and cloud data to find the best viewing location within 1–2 hours of the city. This is your last dedicated aurora opportunity of the trip. Celebrate any sightings with Champagne provided by your guide.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Reykjavík hotel — full Icelandic spread with fresh pastries from a local bakery
meals.lunch: Messinn Restaurant in Reykjavík — celebrated for its exceptional pan-fried fish of the day served in a cast iron skillet with butter and herbs; a true Reykjavík institution
meals.dinner: Grillið Restaurant at Radisson Blu Saga Hotel — rooftop fine dining with panoramic Reykjavík views; exceptional Icelandic beef, fresh seafood, and an award-winning wine list

day_by_day.notes: Whale watching in January is weather-dependent — tours may be cancelled in rough seas. Book with a company that offers a free rescheduling or refund policy. Dress in extreme warmth for the boat — the wind chill on the water is intense. The aurora tour is best booked for 21:00–23:00 when darkness is deepest. Confirm your aurora tour booking 24 hours in advance based on the forecast.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Enjoy a leisurely farewell breakfast at your Reykjavík hotel. Take a last walk along the Reykjavík Old Harbour waterfront and browse the Kolaportið flea market (open weekends) or the boutique shops on Skólavörðustígur for premium Icelandic souvenirs — hand-knitted lopapeysa wool sweaters, Icelandic sea salt, premium skyr, and local design items.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Perlan Museum — a stunning glass-domed building on Öskjuhlíð hill offering a real indoor ice cave experience, a planetarium aurora show, and panoramic 360-degree views of Reykjavík and the surrounding mountains and ocean. This is an excellent final Icelandic experience that encapsulates the country's natural wonders.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer to Keflavík International Airport (approximately 45 minutes from Reykjavík). Depart Iceland with extraordinary memories of aurora borealis, geothermal waters, glaciers, and the raw, elemental beauty of the North Atlantic's most remarkable island.

meals.breakfast: Extended farewell breakfast at your Reykjavík hotel — savour every last bite of Icelandic skyr, smoked salmon, and freshly baked rúgbrauð (dark rye bread)
meals.lunch: Brunch at Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja — traditional Icelandic open-faced sandwiches (smoked lamb, herring, hákarl if you're adventurous), rye bread ice cream, and Icelandic beer
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Keflavík — Fljúgandi Fiskurinn (Flying Fish) restaurant in the terminal offers surprisingly good fresh Icelandic seafood; alternatively, enjoy a final Brennivín schnapps at the airport bar as a proper Icelandic farewell

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in, security, and duty-free shopping at Keflavík. The duty-free store at Keflavík is excellent for premium Icelandic spirits, chocolates, and skincare products at competitive prices — stock up on Icelandic gin, Brennivín, and Blue Lagoon skincare products. Ensure your private transfer is booked for the correct departure time. Skál — cheers to an unforgettable Icelandic adventure!
